transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi… thanks. I guess the main thing is work. I’m an RN, and on the floor I keep losing my train of thought, more than I feel like I should. Like, I’ll be working through a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps, or someone asks another nurse a question nearby, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I’m just… blanking on what I was doing.

I know it’s a busy environment and everyone gets interrupted, so I don’t want to overstate it, but it’s been happening a lot and it’s starting to worry me. Does that make sense?
Thinking back to when you were a child, did you also have this kind of trouble staying focused?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I did well enough in school, so I always kind of framed it as “I’m just scattered,” not anything serious.

But even in elementary school, teachers would write things like I was bright but careless. I was always losing worksheets or forgetting to turn in homework, even if I had done it. My mom basically had to sit with me every night to keep me on track. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work, do you also have this kind of trouble staying focused in your day-to-day life?

Yeah… I mean, outside of work it happens too, but the reason I’m here is really the work part. On the floor it’s just so constant — I’ll be in the middle of thinking through a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps, or someone asks a question nearby, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I’ve completely lost what I was doing.

I know that sounds like normal nursing chaos, and maybe it is to some extent, but it feels like I get knocked off track really easily. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
When this happens at work, do you usually feel anxious right beforehand?

Um… not usually, I don’t think. I mean, I might feel stressed after, when I realize I’ve lost my place or I’m worried I missed something, but right beforehand it doesn’t really feel like anxiety is what starts it.

It’s more like something grabs my attention and then I’m just off track. But I’m not sure if I’m explaining that right.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in the sense of like, I can’t sit still or I’m always needing to move.

I mean, I might shift around a bit if I’m sitting for a long time, but I’ve never really thought of myself as restless. The focus thing feels more like my mind gets pulled away, if that makes sense. Is that okay to say?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t think so… not depressed, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, and tired, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling down in that way.

Unless you mean something broader by depressed? I just don’t want to answer it wrong.
Do these attention problems cause real difficulties for you at home or in other parts of your life outside of work?

Um… outside of work, I guess I notice it, but the biggest impact is honestly at work. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s gotten serious enough that I’m on formal supervision now.

And with charge-nurse tasks, other nurses have had to double-check parts of my follow-through. That’s… hard to say, because I’m supposed to be someone people can rely on. It makes me feel like I’m becoming more of a liability than a leader, which is really upsetting. Is that the kind of difficulty you mean?
Do you often get distracted by things going on around you, even when you’re trying to stay focused?

Yes… I think that’s actually one of the main reasons I’m here.

At work, on the floor, I’ll be trying to keep track of a patient flow issue or what I was about to follow up on, and then an IV pump beeps, or a call light goes off, or someone nearby asks another nurse a question, and it’s like my train of thought just disappears. I don’t mean to be careless, but I’ll suddenly be standing there trying to remember what I was just doing.

I feel bad saying that, because those are normal things on a unit, and I should be able to handle them. But yes, I do get distracted by them. Is that what you mean?
Have these focus problems been present continuously since childhood?

I think… yes, probably. I don’t want to overstate it, because I did well in school in some ways, but even in elementary school my teachers would write things like I was bright but careless.

I was always losing worksheets or forgetting to turn in homework, and my mom had to sit with me every night to keep me on track. So it wasn’t new, exactly… I just maybe learned to compensate for it for a long time. Is that the kind of history you’re asking about?
Did these concentration problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful event in your life?

I’m not sure I can point to one specific stressful event where it suddenly got worse.

It feels more like it’s been there for a long time, and then certain periods make it harder to manage, if that makes sense. I don’t want to blame it on stress if that’s not accurate. I just can’t think of a single event where I’d say, “after that, my concentration changed.” Is that helpful?
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks or keeping track of what you need to do?

Yes… I do. I mean, I try really hard to be organized, so it’s not like I’m not making lists.

When I’m charge nurse, I’ll have scraps of paper, sticky notes, half-started lists—kind of everywhere—and somehow I still can’t always figure out what needs to happen first. I end up responding to whatever issue is the loudest or most urgent in the moment, and then near the end of the shift I’m rushing to catch up on things I should’ve kept track of earlier.

I hate admitting that, because I know it sounds messy. But yes, keeping tasks organized and prioritized is a real problem for me.
Have these attention and organization problems caused clear problems for you at home?

At home… I mean, yes, it does cause problems, though I guess the clearest consequences have been more at work.

I feel bad saying that, because I know you asked about home specifically. At work it’s gotten serious enough that I’m on formal supervision now, and other nurses have to double-check parts of my follow-through when I’m charge nurse. That’s been really hard to admit, because I’m supposed to be the person leading, not someone people are worried might miss something.

So… at home it’s frustrating, but the bigger, clearer impairment is that I feel like I’m becoming a liability instead of a leader. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?

I don’t think so… not in the sense of worrying about everything all the time when nothing is happening.

I mean, I worry when there’s something specific going on, especially if I’m afraid I missed something or I need to follow up on something, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly worrying about lots of unrelated things for no reason. At least, I don’t think that’s the main issue for me. Does that make sense?
At home, do these attention problems cause you clear difficulties?

Honestly… at home it’s there, but I feel like the really clear problems are showing up more at work.

I know you’re asking about home, and I don’t want to dodge the question, but the part that feels most serious is that at work it’s gotten to the point where I’m on formal supervision. Other nurses have had to double-check parts of my follow-through when I’m charge nurse, which is… embarrassing. I’m supposed to be the one leading, and instead I feel like people are worried I’ll miss something.

So at home, yes, it’s difficult, but the clearest impairment is that I feel like I’m becoming more of a liability than a leader.
At home, have these focus and organization problems caused you to miss bills, appointments, or household responsibilities?

Yes… I mean, not constantly, but yes, it has happened.

I’ve forgotten things that really should be routine, like paying a bill or showing up for an appointment, even when I fully intended to do it. Sometimes I’ll set a reminder and still somehow miss the follow-through, which is embarrassing to admit.

It also happens with things like meaning to call a family member back and then realizing days later that I never did. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s enough that it causes problems.
Have these attention problems caused clear difficulties in your relationships?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I don’t think it’s caused, like, major relationship problems… at least not that I’d want to overstate.

I think sometimes people close to me get frustrated if I forget to respond or if I seem like I wasn’t fully listening, but I don’t know if I’d call that “clear difficulties.” Maybe mild friction? I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern of inattentive symptoms beginning in childhood and persisting into adulthood across multiple settings, with clear occupational impairment and some home impairment. Confirmed symptoms include distractibility, losing track of tasks, disorganization/prioritization problems, forgetfulness in daily responsibilities, and childhood history of careless mistakes and losing/forgetting schoolwork. Hyperactivity symptoms are denied, supporting an inattentive presentation. Anxiety, depression, and a stress-related onset were not supported as primary explanations.
